## The gap in my plan

A producer is a test too, so it has a warrant that goes stale when the product changes.

| Fact from the grouping | Value |
|---|---|
| Groups | 60 |
| Groups that run a flight, with different inputs | 16 |
| Groups with only one reader | 41 |

If each group had its own producer, the flight code would have 16 dependent producers. That is over your limit. For a group of one, a separate producer also saves nothing: one test goes stale where one did before.

## The correction

For the ten largest groups, one producer each is right, and those are done or in flight.

For the other 50 groups, I will not create 50 producers. Their tests become readers, and their inputs are added to one producer per family of operations. I expect about six families: flight, click, decision, outer loop, judge and fold, and the HTTP entry.

An edit to the flight code would then make about six producer warrants stale, plus any function-calling tests that reach it. I have not yet measured that figure.

Each family's producer file is edited by one packet at a time, so the families run in parallel and the packets within a family run in sequence.

## Three risks

**The first family may be the least useful to the machine.** The go-ahead family describes what the operator does: approve, ratify, say yes. The machine's aim is to work while you sleep, when no operator turn exists. A guard of "an offer is pending and the operator approves" can never hold in an unattended flight. Families where your turn corrects agent work would give guards on the work itself. Going by my own memory file, those exist in your turns: read the clock before logging a time, supply the missing thing in place of weakening the test. I have not checked how 象 labelled them. The go-ahead family is still a fair first test of the induction method, since it has the most data.

**Merges and splits change names the machine has recorded.** The machine's receipts cite pattern ids and pin the library by hash. If two patterns merge, an old receipt must still resolve. The mission's rule that nothing is deleted covers this only if a merged id stays resolvable as an alias. I met the same problem today from the other side: a rule added later made an older cohort record unreadable.

**Proxies can become guards.** The mission counts proxies separately, which is right. A rule induced from a proxy fact should carry that mark through to the machine, so the machine does not treat "probably an offer was pending" as observed.
